title: Cloud Security Fundamentals

header.html: 5. Trust and security with Google Cloud (about 18%)

5.1 Describe fundamental cloud security concepts: cybersecurity threats and business implications; cloud security versus on-premises security; control, compliance, confidentiality, integrity and availability; key security terms; encryption in use, in transit and at rest; authentication, authorization and auditing; security operations (SecOps) terms
the official Google Cloud Digital Leader exam guide

toc.title: Encryption states and the three As

html:
1Threats and their business impact

Threat What it is Business impact
DDoS Flood of traffic that overwhelms a service Outage, lost sales
Ransomware Malware that encrypts data and demands payment Downtime, ransom, data loss
Cryptomining Stolen computing power used to mine cryptocurrency Surprise cloud bills, slow systems
Malware and viruses Harmful software Data theft, damage
Phishing Fake messages that steal credentials Account takeover, breaches
Misconfiguration Wrong settings, such as a public storage bucket Data exposure
Unsecured third-party systems Weak partners or suppliers Supply chain breaches
Physical damage Fire, flood, theft Hardware and data loss
LLM attacks Attacks on AI models, such as prompt injection and data leakage Wrong answers, leaked data
Exam tip

. Misconfiguration is one of the most common causes of cloud breaches. It is a customer responsibility.

2Cloud security versus on-premises security

On-premises Cloud
You secure everything, including buildings and hardware Shared responsibility: the provider secures the infrastructure, you secure your data, identities and settings
Security tools bought and maintained by you Built-in, always-updated security at scale
Slow to patch Provider patches the platform

3Core security ideas

Idea Meaning
Control You decide who accesses your data and where it lives
Compliance Meeting laws and standards
Confidentiality Only authorized people can read data
Integrity Data stays accurate and unaltered
Availability Systems are there when needed
Key term Meaning
Data loss prevention (DLP) Find and protect sensitive data from leaking
Privileged access Powerful accounts that need extra protection
Least privilege Only the access needed for the job
Zero-trust architecture Never trust, always verify, whatever the network location
Security by default Systems are safe out of the box
Security posture The overall state of security: settings, controls, risks
Cyber resilience Ability to withstand and recover from attacks
Firewall Allows or blocks traffic by rules
Encryption and decryption Scramble data with a key; unscramble it with a key

4Encryption states and the three As

Data state Meaning Protection
At rest Stored on disks and in databases Encrypt storage
In transit Moving across networks Encrypt connections (TLS)
In use Being processed in memory Confidential Computing (Module 11)
A Question Example
Authentication Who are you? Password plus two-step verification or multi-factor authentication
Authorization What may you do? Identity and Access Management (IAM) roles
Auditing What did you do? Logs of actions

5Security operations (SecOps) terms

Term Meaning
Security posture The current security state of the environment
Threat intelligence Knowledge about attackers, their methods and indicators
Threat response Detecting, investigating and fixing an attack
Exam tip

. Authentication = who, authorization = what, auditing = what happened. Two-step verification and MFA strengthen authentication; IAM handles authorization.

Exam tip

. Match the threat to its symptom: outage from traffic = DDoS, locked files and a ransom note = ransomware, huge unexpected compute bill = cryptomining, exposed bucket = misconfiguration.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A company's storage bucket is public by mistake and customer data is exposed. Which threat is this?

  • ADDoS, a flood of network traffic
  • BMisconfiguration, a wrong setting
  • CPhishing, a fake message to steal credentials
  • DCryptomining, stolen computing power
Show the answer

Answer: B. A wrongly configured storage setting is a misconfiguration.

S2Attackers send a flood of traffic that makes the web shop unavailable. Which threat is this?

  • ARansomware, which encrypts the data
  • BPhishing, which steals passwords
  • CDDoS, which overwhelms a service
  • DPhysical damage, which destroys hardware
Show the answer

Answer: C. A flood of traffic that takes a service offline is a distributed denial-of-service attack.

S3A user logs in with a password and a code from a phone app. Which security idea is strengthened?

  • AAuthentication, which proves who the user is
  • BAuthorization, which decides what the user may do
  • CAuditing, which records what the user did
  • DEncryption at rest, which protects stored data
Show the answer

Answer: A. Two-step verification strengthens authentication.

S4Which control decides which actions a signed-in user may perform on a resource?

  • AIdentity and Access Management roles
  • BTwo-step verification codes for each sign-in
  • CTransport encryption for traffic
  • DCloud Storage Archive class
Show the answer

Answer: A. IAM roles handle authorization, which decides what a user may do.

S5Customer data is encrypted on its disk and also while it travels between services. Which two states are covered?

  • AAt rest and in transit
  • BIn use and at rest only
  • CIn use and in transit only
  • DNeither, because encryption covers one state
Show the answer

Answer: A. Encrypting stored data protects data at rest; encrypting connections protects data in transit.

S6Which statement describes zero-trust architecture?

  • AUsers on the office network are always trusted
  • BOnly the perimeter firewall needs protection
  • CNever trust, always verify, whatever the location
  • DA VPN login grants full trust to the connected device
Show the answer

Answer: C. Zero trust verifies every request and does not trust any location by default.

6.2 Recall questions

R1What does ransomware do?

Show the answer

Encrypts data and demands payment.

R2What is least privilege?

Show the answer

Only the access needed for the job.

R3What are the three data states for encryption?

Show the answer

At rest, in transit, in use.

R4What does authentication answer?

Show the answer

Who are you?

R5What is security posture?

Show the answer

The overall state of security.

R6What is threat intelligence?

Show the answer

Knowledge about attackers and their methods.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Threats DDoS, ransomware, cryptomining, malware, phishing, misconfiguration, third parties, LLM attacks
Cloud vs on-premises shared responsibility; built-in security; provider patches the platform
Ideas control, compliance, CIA; least privilege, zero trust, posture, resilience
Encryption at rest, in transit, in use
Three As authentication (two-step verification, MFA), authorization (IAM), auditing (logs)
